title: Text Field
description: Public API, focused editing, semantic input hints, icons, accessibility, and platform behaviour for Firstlight Text Field.

blocks.text:
Text Field enters and edits one line of text using the native field, keyboard,
autofill, selection, and accessibility behaviour of each platform.

<firstlight:text-field
    label="Email"
    placeholder="you@example.com"
    helper="Used for appointment updates."
    keyboard="email"
    content-type="email"
    autocapitalize="none"
    :autocorrect="false"
    clearable
    native:model.blur="email"
/>

blocks.label: value / native:model
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Published PHP value; omission defaults to ''.

blocks.label: label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Visible label and accessibility-name fallback.

blocks.label: placeholder
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Short example; never a replacement for a label.

blocks.label: helper
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Supporting guidance below the field.

blocks.label: error
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Validation feedback that replaces helper text.

blocks.label: required
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Communicates required metadata without performing validation.

blocks.label: disabled
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Prevents focus, editing, and every action.

blocks.label: read-only
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Allows native selection and copy while preventing edits and changes.

blocks.label: keyboard
blocks.text:
Accepted type: enum string
Purpose: text, email, phone, url, number, or decimal.

blocks.label: content-type
blocks.text:
Accepted type: enum string
Purpose: name, username, email, password, new-password, or one-time-code.

blocks.label: secure
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Masks display without changing the stored string.

blocks.label: autocapitalize
blocks.text:
Accepted type: enum string
Purpose: none, sentences, words, or characters; omission keeps platform policy.

blocks.label: autocorrect
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Explicitly enables or disables platform autocorrection.

blocks.label: submit-label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: enum string
Purpose: done, go, next, search, or send; omission keeps the platform default.

blocks.label: leading-icon
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Shared decorative leading icon fallback.

blocks.label: leading-icon-ios
blocks.text:
Accepted type: `IosSymbol
Purpose: string`

blocks.label: leading-icon-android
blocks.text:
Accepted type: `AndroidSymbol
Purpose: string`

blocks.label: trailing-icon
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Shared decorative or authored-action icon fallback.

blocks.label: trailing-icon-ios
blocks.text:
Accepted type: `IosSymbol
Purpose: string`

blocks.label: trailing-icon-android
blocks.text:
Accepted type: `AndroidSymbol
Purpose: string`

blocks.label: trailing-a11y-label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Required accessible name when trailing-icon has @press.

blocks.label: clearable
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Adds a native clear action while editable text is non-empty. The clear accessibility label is package chrome; see Localize chrome.

blocks.label: revealable
blocks.text:
Accepted type: bool
Purpose: Adds native show/hide password state; requires secure. Show and hide accessibility labels are package chrome; see Localize chrome.

blocks.label: a11y-label
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Explicit accessible name when no visible label is appropriate.

blocks.label: a11y-hint
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: Additional VoiceOver and TalkBack guidance.

blocks.label: class
blocks.text:
Accepted type: string
Purpose: External EDGE layout for the complete field.

Plain native:model and .live publish while editing. .blur and .lazy
publish on focus loss or submit. .debounce.500ms publishes after the quiet
period and flushes on blur or submit; durations below 50 ms are rejected.
Native typing, selection, cursor position, and marked-text composition remain
local while focused so PHP acknowledgements do not cause keyboard jumps.

On iOS, pressing a <firstlight:button> while the field is focused publishes
its pending .blur or .debounce change before the press, so the handler reads
the current value. Icon Button and List Item presses do not flush the field
first. On Android, blur/debounce changes are not yet guaranteed to reach PHP
before a button press, so for forms submitted by a separate button use
native:model.live="email" (or plain native:model). A button press is not the
field's @submit event; for keyboard submission, the field's own @submit
handler receives the current string directly.

The shared icon is the fallback; the active platform override wins. Blade uses
the exact -ios and -android suffixes above, and typed Android symbols retain
their filled or outlined variant on the wire. Decorative icons are silent.

An authored trailing action requires all of trailing-icon,
trailing-a11y-label, and @press. clearable and revealable instead own
their platform-native icon and localized accessibility state. These semantic
actions are mutually exclusive and cannot share the trailing slot with an
authored action.

Clearing retains focus and immediately publishes '' through @change, even
under blur or debounce sync. Revealing changes presentation only and never
publishes the password value.

Contract exceptions still reject invalid types, unsupported enums, incomplete
trailing actions, and conflicting affordances before publication. User
validation is separate: screens that use ValidatesFields auto-bind the first
MessageBag message for the field's native:model or error-for name. An
authored error wins. required is display metadata and does not run Laravel
rules. See Validate fields.

Error text replaces helper text without replacing the field's accessible name
or value. Decorative icons stay hidden from assistive technology. Icon actions
are separate native accessibility nodes with a minimum 44-point target on iOS
and 48-dp target on Android. A visible label or explicit a11y-label is
required during development.

The editable input uses a11y-label when supplied, otherwise label, in both
plain and secure presentation; a11y-hint remains additional guidance rather
than replacing the name.

iOS uses an Apple SwiftUI TextField or SecureField composition with system
field treatment, SF Symbols, Dynamic Type, native keyboard and autofill hints,
and Apple spacing. Android uses Material 3 OutlinedTextField, Material label
and supporting/error slots, TextFieldValue selection and composition,
keyboard/IME options, and Compose autofill content types.
